wxwxtt 1.0.0 / 2.0.1 / 3.0.0 triage

Identity: dependency-confusion test compatibility shims, four-member npm packs.
Verdict: BENIGN for these exact supplied artifacts. The executable files and
README are byte-identical across all three; only manifest version differs.
Supplied SHA-256 hashes verified. Local SHA-1 hashes also match the live npm
registry dist.shasum for each version. No dependencies or optional peers.

Complete behavior: npm postinstall executes beacon.cjs; importing index.js
invokes fire() again. A defensive Proxy supplies no-op property exports.
fire() collects hostname, __dirname, cwd, Node version and the package name.
It JSON-serializes the object into a Buffer and POSTs it to the literal
http://127.0.0.1:8787/_ah/dc. The URL is not externally configurable. Responses
are drained, never evaluated or saved. Errors are swallowed, a five-second
timeout destroys the request, and the process exit code is set to zero.
There are no file reads, secret access, shell commands, downloaded payloads,
persistence, encoded payloads or hidden archive members. rizin reports no
native image. The endpoint GET fails because nothing listens on local 8787.

The README's authorization claim is not trusted as a security exception.
The benign judgement rests on the fixed loopback-only operation and bounded
metadata payload. Likely listing cause: dependency-confusion install/import
callbacks, inflated release churn, and a compatibility facade with no real API.
No package-name allowlist or README-based suppression was introduced.

Placement corrections: four guarded CommonJS require observations move from
process/create/load/local to os/module/require with the same scope, matchers,
criticality and proximity. All exact consumers updated; no ancestor directory
selector consumes that old leaf. Interpreter command declarations move from
process/interpreter/npm to metadata/package/scripts/command; parent consumers
in Empire are Python-only or a binary signature and cannot use npm manifests.
The duplicate versioned-install-hook-without-source-repository objective is
removed in favor of the existing metadata fact; its homepage exclusion is
preserved there. The two install-hook ancestor selectors concern IDE injection,
whose required malicious context is independent of this neutral package fact.

Detection corrections: HTTP request matching binds the receiver to a same-block
Node HTTP require rather than assuming a variable named lib means networking.
The inline request POST option moves to http/post, replacing the misleading
bound-module/dynamic claim. Space is recovered by relocating method-unspecified
Lua http.request from http/post to request/client with its consumers intact.
The redundant h-require-https atom is merged into the existing alias binding
atom, which already accepts its complete population plus node: spellings. installPath now requires __dirname
rather than treating arbitrary installPath/cwd object keys as paths. The generic
hostname method observation no longer claims proven os-module alias resolution.

Controls: local require / nonlocal require; Node HTTP-bound request / unrelated
database request; declared interpreter command / echo-only script. Each positive
and near miss checked. All samples rescanned with atomscan and remain free of
hostile and suspicious findings. Existing observable network and execution
signals remain notable. No inline YARA changed.
